content.text: In the musicplayerdemo it is possible to navigagte to the tracklist by tabbing. But when the tracklist is in focus, it is not possible to navigate it by keyboard. That would be a natural thing. Is that nrmally supported by swiftui? How can we do so similarly?
I'll research how keyboard navigation works in the demo and what SwiftUI does for lists.

2. **Do not re-report events for skipped writes.** Because the write was not
   applied, no change signal fires and no `VALUE_CHANGED` is re-emitted — the
   echo loop is broken at the source.
3. **Resume on session end.** When the interaction ends (release / blur), the

This is **renderer state, not application state** (see
[ADR-0003](../docs/decisions/0003-application-state-and-delta-emission.md)): the
in-edit value is transient input/rendered-output state, like the scroll offset
and the text caret.

The session boundaries are also **reported as events** so the application can
suppress echoes of *derived* state the renderer cannot know about (a custom
drag offset, a drawn position):

- `FOCUS_CHANGED` (0x08) — the control gained/lost focus.
- `EDITING_CHANGED` (0x09) — a value/text edit session started/ended.

Both are reported **only when the target declared the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS`
bit** (`FOCUS` = `1<<5`, `EDITING` = `1<<6`). An application that observes
`EDITING_CHANGED { editing: true }` should hold back authoritative echoes of the
edited state until `{ editing: false }`.

The mechanism is **per-state / per-session**: implemented today for value drags
(`SLIDER`); text editing and other continuous inputs use the same path.

### Target resolution

The renderer resolves `targetId` from its own rendered-output tree (its
`id → native element` map): the event's position is hit-tested against that
tree to find the deepest node with the matching listener bit. If no listener is
declared, the event is not reported.

### Transport paths

| Path | Mechanism |
|------|-----------|
| Shared memory (desktop/native) | The host writes `EVENT` opcodes into the event ring (host → guest) at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains at `eventReadCursor`. Events are consumed as written (no frame batching). |
| Network batch (SSR → browser) | Host → guest batches use the `0x0001` direction flag of the `PLPL` batch format (see OPCODE.md Transport) |

### Encoding

Every event is a 16-byte opcode:

```
[Category=0x03][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
```

`TEXT_CHANGED` is the exception: its payload is an offset into the host → guest
event arena (shared memory) or the batch's string section (network), so it is
only fully decodable with that string source (the same convention as
`PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`).

## Core event catalog

### Pointer

Pointer events carry a viewport-relative point in **logical points** (`B`=x,
`C`=y, f32).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `POINTER_DOWN` | 0x01 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | press (basis of `onTapGesture`, `Button` action) |
| `POINTER_MOVE` | 0x02 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` (0x0001) / `HOVER_LEAVE` (0x0002) | hover/enter/leave, drag basis |
| `POINTER_UP` | 0x03 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | release (basis of `onTapGesture`) |

- **Flags**:
  - `POINTER_SECONDARY`: the secondary button (right mouse, long-press) rather
    than the primary.
  - `HOVER_ENTER` (bit 0 of `POINTER_MOVE`): the pointer just entered the
    node's bounds (is now hovering). `HOVER_LEAVE` (bit 1): the pointer just
    left. A plain move has neither bit set.
- **Listener bits**: `POINTER_DOWN` (bit 0), `POINTER_MOVE` (bit 1),
  `POINTER_UP` (bit 2).
- **Renderer**: attaches native press/hover recognition to the matching native
  element when the listener bit is set. Multiple pointer events may be reported
  for one physical gesture (down → several moves → up), all for the same
  `targetId` while the pointer stays over the node.

### Keyboard

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `KEY_DOWN` | 0x04 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` (0x0002) | `onKeyPress(.down)` |
| `KEY_UP` | 0x05 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | `onKeyPress(.up)` |

- **`keyCode`**: a **canonical, platform-independent logical key code** (a
  renderer maps native scancodes/key-codes onto this canonical set). The
  canonical set (letters/digits/arrows/Enter/Tab/…) is renderer-shared and
  documented in the conformance vectors.
- **`modifiers`**: u8 bitmask — `Shift`=0x01, `Control`=0x02, `Alt`=0x04,
  `Meta/Super`=0x08.
- **`KEY_REPEAT`**: bit 1 of flags; set when the key is an OS auto-repeat.
- **Listener bits**: `KEY_DOWN` (bit 3), `KEY_UP` (bit 4).
- **Focus**: keyboard events are reported to the focused node (the node that
  most recently gained focus), or to the node that declared the listener and
  has keyboard focus. See `FOCUS_CHANGED` below.

### Value

Value events carry a control's semantic value, resolved by the renderer from
its own native control geometry.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `VALUE_CHANGED` | 0x06 | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`Toggle`/`Picker`/`Menu` binding changes |

- **Semantics per control** (see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) controls):
  - `SLIDER`/`STEPPER`/`GAUGE` — the numeric value in the control's range.
  - `TOGGLE` — 0/1 (checked state; the same value the app writes to
    `SELECTED`).
  - `PICKER`/`MENU` — the selected option/action-item index.
  - `COLOR_PICKER` — the packed `0xAARRGGBB` color reinterpreted as an f32 bit
    pattern.
  - `DATE_PICKER` uses the dedicated `DATE_CHANGED` event below (its value is
    two fields and does not fit `VALUE_CHANGED`).
- The app writes the received value into its bound `State`; the engine's
  signal flush re-emits the `SET_PROPERTY` delta back to the renderer (the
  renderer reflects its own native control).
- **No listener bit**: value-bearing controls are reported by the renderer by
  virtue of their component type, but still gated by the transport-aware event
  guards (a control without `BINDING_ID` reports nothing). The renderer owns
  the gesture (e.g. slider drag) that produces them.

### Date

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `DATE_CHANGED` | 0x0D | targetId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | `DatePicker` value binding |

- The date is encoded as two 32-bit fields — `B` = **days since epoch**
  (signed I32; pre-1970 is negative) and `C` = **millis of day** (U32,
  0..86,400,000) — matching the `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` command (OPCODE.md). No
  string/arena indirection: the event is fully inline. It works over the
  shared-memory ring today and will use the same inline encoding for host →
  guest network batches once that direction lands (see OPCODE.md Transport).
- **No listener bit**: like `VALUE_CHANGED`, reported by virtue of the
  component type.

### Text

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `TEXT_CHANGED` | 0x07 | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | `TextField` value binding |
| `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 0x08 | targetId | focused (0/1) | 0 | — | `@FocusState` |
| `EDITING_CHANGED` | 0x09 | targetId | editing (0/1) | 0 | — | `TextField`/`Slider` `onEditingChanged` |
| `SUBMIT` | 0x0A | targetId | 0 | 0 | — | `TextField` `onSubmit` / `onCommit` |

- **`TEXT_CHANGED`**: the new text is a length-prefixed entry
  (`[u32 byteLength][bytes…]`). Over the **shared-memory ring** the renderer
  bump-allocates it into the host-owned **event arena** and `B` is its absolute
  offset (see OPCODE.md); over the **network** it lives in the batch's string
  section referenced by a *relative* `B` offset — exactly the `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`
  dual convention. A bare opcode cannot resolve the text; batch-aware decoders
  (`pathland-core-transport`, Java `FrameCodec`, TS `decoder.ts`) resolve it.
  The event is reported on **every** edit, including intermediate edits, not
  only on commit.
- **`FOCUS_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 gained focus, 0 lost focus. The renderer reports
  it for nodes that declared the `FOCUS` listener bit (bit 5). Focus is what
  routes subsequent `KEY_*` events.
- **`EDITING_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 editing session began, 0 ended. Reported for
  nodes that declared the `EDITING` listener bit (bit 6).
- **`SUBMIT`**: the user committed the field (Enter). Reported for nodes that
  declared the `SUBMIT` listener bit (bit 7). `B` MAY carry the current text as
  a string-section offset (reserved for future use; 0 today).

### Scroll

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `SCROLL` | 0x0B | targetId | offsetX (f32) | offsetY (f32) | — | `ScrollView` offset, `onScrollPhaseChange` |
| `WHEEL` | 0x0C | targetId | deltaX (f32) | deltaY (f32) | — | `onScrollWheelEvent` / trackpad |

- **`SCROLL`**: the content offset of a `SCROLLVIEW` (logical points), reported
  for nodes that declared the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8). The renderer
  reports the absolute offset after each scroll delta.
- **`WHEEL`**: raw wheel/trackpad deltas (logical points), reported for nodes
  that declared the `WHEEL` listener bit (bit 9). Renderers map native scroll

## 5. Interaction & State

Semantic properties controlling whether and how an element responds to input,
plus accessibility. These are the "semantic" (`0x2000`) properties.

| SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property | Type | Emission |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ------ | ---------- |
| `.hidden()` | `VISIBLE` 0x100E | U8 (0 = hidden) | one |
| `.disabled(_:)` | `ENABLED` 0x2003 | U8 (1 = enabled) | one |
| `.allowsHitTesting(_:)` | `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING` 0x102F | U8 (0/1) | one |
| `.controlSize(_:)` | `CONTROL_SIZE` 0x200C | ENUM (`Small`=0, `Regular`=1, `Large`=2) | one |
| `.focusable(_:)` | — (via `FOCUS` listener) | — | none (declares `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit 5) |
| `.accessibilityLabel(_:)` | `LABEL` 0x200A | STRING | one (arenaRef) |
| `.accessibilityRole(_:)` | `ROLE` 0x2001 | ENUM | one |
| `.accessibilityState(_:)` | `STATE` 0x2002 | ENUM | one |

### Semantics

- **`VISIBLE`**: 0 hides the element entirely (removed from layout and hit
  testing by the renderer); 1 shows it. Diff-based emission means toggling
  visibility emits a single `SET_PROPERTY`.
- **`ENABLED`** is the inverse of SwiftUI `.disabled()`: 1 = interactive, 0 =
  disabled. Disabled controls do not emit events.
- **Icons** ([`ICON`](./PRIMITIVES.md#icon--icon-0x0b), spec/ICONS.md): the
  `ICON_NAME` string selects a renderer-native symbol; it is **not** an asset
  reference (`IMAGE_SOURCE`). `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE`
  size and tint it like text; `LABEL` makes it presentable.
- **`.focusable`** has no property: the app requests focus events via the
  `FOCUS` listener bit (`EVENT_LISTENERS`, bit 5) and observes
  `EVENT::FOCUS_CHANGED` — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md).
- **`ROLE`** is **semantic structure only** — its enumerated values are defined
  in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#semantic-properties), not here. Interactive/control
  roles (button, link, checkbox, …) are **not roles**: they are intrinsic to the
  control components (a `BUTTON` is an interactive button element, a `TOGGLE` a
  checkbox/switch, a `MENU` a menu), and a custom-looking button uses `Button` +
  `ButtonStyle`. The DSL rejects role codes outside the semantic catalog.
- **`STATE`** is a semantic accessibility property — it never describes visual
  styling.
- **`.font(_:)`** is the single font modifier (SwiftUI `Font`): a predefined
  typography (`Font.headline()` → `TEXT_STYLE`), a custom family + size
  (`Font.custom(name, size)` → `FONT_FAMILY` + `FONT_SIZE`), or a system
  size/weight/design (`Font.system(size, weight, design)` → `FONT_SIZE` +
---

| Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Kotlin DSL | Property(ies) |
|----------|---------------------------|----------|---------------|
| `hidden` | `.hidden()` | `.modifiers(hidden())` / `.modifiers(visible(v -> v.visible(boolean)))` | `VISIBLE` 0x100E |
| `disabled` | `.disabled(_:)` | `.modifiers(disabled(d -> d.disabled(boolean)))` | `ENABLED` 0x2003 (inverse: 1 = interactive) |
| `allowsHitTesting` | `.allowsHitTesting(_:)` | `.modifiers(allowsHitTesting(a -> a.allowed(boolean)))` | `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING` 0x102F |
| `controlSize` | `.controlSize(_:)` | `.modifiers(ControlSize.LARGE)` (the enum *is* the modifier) | `CONTROL_SIZE` 0x200C |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `.accessibilityLabel(_:)` | `.modifiers(accessibilityLabel(a -> a.text(String)))` | `LABEL` 0x200A |
| `accessibilityRole` | `.accessibilityRole(_:)` | `.modifiers(accessibilityRole(a -> a.role(int)))` | `ROLE` 0x2001 |
| `accessibilityState` | `.accessibilityState(_:)` | `.modifiers(accessibilityState(a -> a.state(int)))` | `STATE` 0x2002 |
| `modifier` (custom) | `.modifier(_:)` | `.modifiers(ViewModifier)` | composes core modifiers |
| `buttonStyle` | `.buttonStyle(_:)` | `.modifiers(ButtonStyle)` | environment-scoped (`Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` key, nearest-wins); the style supplies the button's content ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)) |
| `labelStyle` | `.labelStyle(_:)` | `.modifiers(LabelStyle)` | environment-scoped (`Environment.LABEL_STYLE` key, nearest-wins); DSL-only control flow — no wire property |
| `videoStyle` | `.videoStyle(_:)` | `.modifiers(VideoStyle)` | environment-scoped (`Environment.VIDEO_STYLE` key, nearest-wins); the style supplies the `VIDEO` surface's control content ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)) |
| `environment` | `.environment(_:_:)` | `.modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(EnvironmentKey).value(value)))` | environment-scoped (a typed `EnvironmentKey`, nearest-wins); no wire property |
| `windowMetadata` | (platform shell metadata) | `.modifiers(windowMetadata(w -> w.title(signal).description(signal).locale(value)))` | `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` fields (`TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) — renderer maps them to its window chrome |
| `focusable` | `.focusable(_:)` | (via the `PointerEvents` modifier) | **no property** — declares `FOCUS` listener bit 5; observe `FOCUS_CHANGED` |
| raw listeners | `.pointerEvents(mask)` / `.pointer_events(mask)` | `.modifiers(pointerEvents(p -> p.mask(int)))` | `EVENT_LISTENERS` 0x2005 (u32 bitmask, bits per EVENTS.md) |

**Notes**: `visible(boolean)` is a Pathland extra (SwiftUI only has
`.hidden()` — `Visible`/`Hidden`). `accessibilityRole`/`accessibilityState`
take raw `int` codes today rather than a typed enum. Raw input listeners are
exposed through the `PointerEvents` modifier value — there is no per-event sugar
(e.g. a `.focusable` or `.onSubmit` that sets the matching bit). `environment`
is the one inheritance/scoping modifier
([§6 rule 6](#6-authoring-conventions)), alongside the style modifiers.

**Window metadata is root-scoped.** `windowMetadata` applies to the whole
hosting surface, not to the subtree it wraps. Values are signals (a plain value
is wrapped as a constant), so a route's title is a `computed` over the router:
`windowMetadata(w -> w.title(computed(() -> titleFor(router.path()))))`. A
signal change re-emits only that `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` field; the renderer
maps it to the window/tab title and description.

# pathland-render-gtk — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

The **GTK4 renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto native GTK widgets
(shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`. Design-token contract:
`spec/TOKENS.md`.

**Note (2026-09-23):** the toolkit-free decode core (`RenderTree`/`HostNode`,
`apply_frame`, token tables + resolution, `concrete_default_tables`,
`render_tree_from_frame`, `describe`) moved to the shared
`pathland-render-core` crate; this crate now consumes it and keeps the
GTK-specific layers (`tokens.rs` native-theme enrichment, `layout.rs`,
`capi.rs`). `pathland_gtk::RenderTree` etc. remain re-exported for
compatibility.

## Implemented

- **Window metadata**: the GTK window title follows `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` `TITLE` (fallback: the run-time title); `DESCRIPTION` maps to the window accessible description.

- **Components → widgets** (`widget_kind`/`build_widget`):
  - `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` → `GtkBox` (spacing/alignment/
    padding/content-margins),
  - `PROXY_VIEW` (spec/PROXY.md) → `GtkBox` (a transparent container): the spliced
    (id-remapped) origin subtree lays out in place,
  - `TEXT` → `GtkLabel` (text; `TEXT_STYLE`/`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/
    `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_DESIGN`/`COLOR` via a Pango `FontDescription`/
    attributes). `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` renders through Pango **markup**
    (nested spans for the v1 runs + `<a href>` links) because pango 0.20 has
    no link attribute; the plain text stays the fallback,
  - `BUTTON` → `GtkButton` (label; composite body when it has children),
  - `ICON` → `GtkImage` (the canonical `ICON_NAME` maps through this renderer's
    own `gtk_icon_name` map to an Adwaita symbolic icon name; `FONT_SIZE` → pixel size,
    `COLOR` → CSS tint; unmapped names fall back to `image-missing`),
  - `GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` → `GtkGrid` (row-major cells from child
    index + `WIDTH` column count),
  - `SCROLLVIEW` → `GtkScrolledWindow` (single child),
  - `ZSTACK` → `GtkOverlay`,
  - `SPACER` → expanding box, `IMAGE` → `GtkPicture` (`IMAGE_SOURCE`),
  - `TOGGLE` → `GtkSwitch`/`GtkCheckButton`/`GtkToggleButton` by `TOGGLE_STYLE`
    (`SELECTED` ↔ active),
  - `SLIDER` → `GtkScale` (`VALUE`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`STEP`),
  - `TEXT_FIELD` → `GtkEntry` (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`IS_SECURE`),
  - `TEXT_EDITOR` → `GtkTextView` (multi-line),
  - `COLOR` → `GtkDrawingArea` (solid fill), `SHAPE` → `GtkDrawingArea`
    (`SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER` → `GtkSeparator`,
  - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `GtkProgressBar`/`GtkSpinner`,
  - `GAUGE` → `GtkLevelBar`, `STEPPER` → `GtkSpinButton`,
  - `DATE_PICKER` → `GtkCalendar`, `PICKER` → `GtkDropDown` (option children +
    `SELECTION`), `MENU` → `GtkMenuButton`, `COLOR_PICKER` → `GtkColorButton`.
  Unknown components → blank `GtkLabel`.
- **Container + composite reconciliation** (diff-guarded): stacks/grid/scroll/
  overlay children, and **Composite Override Mode** for `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`MENU`
  with children (custom body wrapped in the native button shell). A `BUTTON`
  composite body is a **horizontal row** with centered children (matching the
  HTML renderer's `.pathland-button` `inline-flex`); `TOGGLE`/`MENU` bodies stay
  vertical (HTML wraps those as block/inline-block). A composite control **sizes
  to its content on the main axis** (the button's main-axis `valign`/`halign` is
  `Center`, mirroring HTML's `inline-flex`) unless the node is explicitly
  `FILL`-sized — otherwise the enclosing box's default `Fill` alignment stretches
  it (e.g. a library row button absorbs the viewport height, inflating
  fixed-size images). A **`VIDEO` surface** with children (a custom
  `VideoStyle` body, spec DSL.md §5.7) is a container too: its
  control children reconcile into the media container box. Control-level
  `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE`/`TEXT_STYLE` are
  emitted as CSS (`color`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-family`) so they
  **cascade** to the content's child labels (e.g. `.foregroundStyle`/`.fontSize`
  on a composite Button).
- **Style properties**: `VISIBLE`, `OPACITY`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`,
  `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `PADDING` + per-edge, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`/

---

## Virtual extent (lazy containers)

A `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK`/`LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` that carries
`ITEM_COUNT` (`0x0022`) and `ITEM_EXTENT` (`0x0023`) is a **windowed data
container**. It lays out only the units the application emitted, but occupies
the full list extent so a scroll viewport reports the correct scrollbar and
offsets.

The **window unit** is one item for a stack, one **row** for a `LAZY_VGRID`,
and one **column** for a `LAZY_HGRID`. Let `N = ITEM_COUNT` (unit count),
`E = ITEM_EXTENT` (the unit's main-axis size: item extent, row height, or
column width), `S = max(0, SPACING)` (absent `SPACING` is `0`), and
`F = FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` (default `0`). Windowing requires `E > 0`; an absent or
non-positive `ITEM_EXTENT` means the lazy container is an ordinary eager
container.

- **Virtual extent** — the container's main-axis size is
  `N*E + max(0, N-1)*S`. `N = 0` gives `0`.
- **Item offset** — absolute item `i` starts at `i*(E+S)`.
- **Window placement** — emitted unit `j` is absolute unit `F+j` and starts at
  `(F+j)*(E+S)`. Children are emitted in ascending absolute-unit order. A grid
  unit emits all of its cells (row-major for `LAZY_VGRID`, column-major for
  `LAZY_HGRID`); a stack unit emits one item.
- **Child size** — the container constrains each child to exactly `E` on the
  main axis (a Fixed box; overflow is visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`). The
  cross axis is the ordinary stack contract: the child keeps its size and is
  positioned by `ALIGNMENT`; a `Fill`-sized child stretches on the cross axis.
- **Missing children** — the window need not cover every unit. Units with no
  emitted children are empty virtual space; the renderer never invents rows.
  Emitted children beyond `N` units are ignored.
- **Fill propagation** — the virtual extent is the container's main-axis size;
  it does not propagate `Fill` from a window child on the main axis. Cross-axis
  fill propagation is unchanged.
- **Visible range** — the renderer computes which absolute units intersect the
  nearest scrolling ancestor's viewport (or the root surface when there is
  none). In the lazy container's main-axis content coordinates, with the
  viewport spanning `[viewportStart, viewportEnd)`:
  `first = clamp(floor(viewportStart/(E+S)), 0, N)` and
  `endExclusive = clamp(ceil(viewportEnd/(E+S)), 0, N)`. The range is
  conservative: it may include a partially scrolled item, but never excludes a
  visible one. The renderer reports `EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` for nodes with
  listener bit 10, at most once per frame and only when `(first, endExclusive)`
  changes. A renderer SHOULD report the final range when a scroll gesture ends.
  The engine MAY coalesce successive reports for a target (latest wins) before
  updating the window or a paged data source; a scrollbar jump need not load
  every intermediate window's pages. The final report remains authoritative.
- **Engine prefetch** — the engine MAY add a bounded, directional prefetch
  margin around the reported range, derived from the report velocity (the
  distance between successive reports over elapsed time). The margin is
  engine-owned and not author-configured; a small base margin applies to the
  first report and to slow scrolling. A report with no movement returns to the
  base margin. The application may still emit a larger window.

**Variable item extents.** A lazy **stack** (not a grid) MAY carry
`ITEM_EXTENTS` (`0x0025`, LIST of F32), `FIRST_ITEM_OFFSET` (`0x0026`, F32), and
`TOTAL_EXTENT` (`0x0027`, F32) alongside the fixed properties. When present:

- `ITEM_EXTENTS` holds one main-axis extent per **emitted window item**, in
  window order. `FIRST_ITEM_OFFSET` is the offset of the first emitted item in
  the full content, and `TOTAL_EXTENT` is the full content extent.
- The window starts at `FIRST_ITEM_OFFSET`; each emitted item uses its extent;
  the window extent is `sum(ITEM_EXTENTS) + max(0, k-1)*S`.
- The container's virtual extent is `TOTAL_EXTENT`; the fixed formula is not
  used. `ITEM_EXTENT` remains the **default/estimated** extent for items outside
  the emitted window.
- The renderer computes the visible range by walking the window extents from
  `FIRST_ITEM_OFFSET`; if the viewport lies outside the emitted window, it
  estimates with `ITEM_EXTENT` and reports that estimate so the application can
  emit a covering window.

import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Properties
import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode

/**
 * A view wrapped by `onTapGesture`: declares pointer-down/up listeners and
 * records the tap action on the built node for the emitter's registry.
 */
internal class TapGestureView(private val content: View, private val action: Runnable?) : View {
    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
        val node = content.renderNode(env)
        val existing = node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS]
        val mask = if (existing is Int) existing else 0
        node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS] =
            mask or Commands.Listeners.POINTER_DOWN or Commands.Listeners.POINTER_UP
        if (action != null) node.tapActions.add(action)
        return node
    }
}

/**
 * Protocol semantic-role codes for the `ROLE` property.
 *
 * These describe document structure (heading, list, listitem, navigation,
 * main, …), not interactivity: buttons/toggles/sliders carry their control role
 * intrinsically. The renderer maps a code to its native semantic element.
 */
object Roles {
    const val NONE = 0
    const val HEADER = 1
    const val PARAGRAPH = 2
    const val LIST = 3
    const val LIST_ITEM = 4
    const val SUMMARY = 5
    const val BANNER = 6
    const val NAVIGATION = 7
    const val MAIN = 8
    const val CONTENT_INFO = 9
    const val COMPLEMENTARY = 10
    const val ARTICLE = 11
    const val SECTION = 12
    const val SEARCH = 13

    /** Whether [code] is a defined semantic role. */
    fun isDefined(code: Int): Boolean = code in NONE..SEARCH
}

# @pathland/dom-renderer

The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A small, vanilla-TypeScript
hydration client (zero runtime dependencies) that:

- **Hydrates** the server-rendered DOM by `data-pathland-id`.
- **Decodes** self-contained `PLPL` opcode batches (bounds-checked) and applies
  them in place: **`STYLE` deltas** (the full property catalog — layout, text,
  styling, effects, semantic/control variants, plus `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` →
  CSS variables) and **`TREE` deltas** (create/delete/insert/remove/move —
  runtime structural updates without a full reload).
- **Reports raw inputs** back over WebSocket as `EVENT` batches — the full event
  catalog (pointer down/move/up, key down/up, value/text/date changed, focus/
  editing, submit, scroll, wheel) — guest → host (flags `0x0000`), gated by the
  SSR `EVENT_LISTENERS` mask.
- **Negotiates** the protocol version (mismatch → reload) and **reconnects**
  with exponential backoff.

Styling is renderer-owned: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic. The SSR HTML
carries a Tailwind-derived preflight plus a tokenized built-in design system
(`--pl-*` CSS variables); per-node values are inline style, with literal colors
inline and semantic design tokens as CSS variables. Native browser controls
inherit the same preflight + design tokens through `.pathland-*` classes. The
DOM renderer owns the bounded property → style map (`src/classes.ts`).

## Layout

```
src/
  constants.ts   protocol constants (mirror spec/)
  plpl.ts        bounds-checked batch parse + string decode
  format.ts      f32/ARGB/date/float formatting
  elements.ts    component → DOM shell factory (TREE create)
  classes.ts     Option A style/state appliers (inline style + ARIA + CSS vars)
  apply.ts       delta application (STYLE + TREE) over the id → Node registry
  events.ts      guest → host EVENT encoders
  transport.ts   WebSocket connect/reconnect/version negotiation
  index.ts       bootstrap (hydrate + connect + listeners)
```

## Build & test

```bash
npm ci
npm test          # vitest (happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE apply, transport
npm run build     # tsc --noEmit + esbuild -> dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js (IIFE, minified)
npm run copy-to-libs    # copy the bundle into the framework libraries' static dirs
```

The per-window-id service worker has a real-browser E2E (Chromium + WebKit) — the
worker-engine differences (e.g. WebKit reporting an empty `clientId` on navigations)
are invisible to jsdom, so they are guarded here:

```bash
npx playwright install chromium webkit   # one-time
npm run test:e2e                          # boots a fixture server + the shipped sw.js
```

## The bundle

`dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` ships in the Spring Boot starter and the Quarkus
extension under a content-hashed name — `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (copied into each
library's static resources by `npm run copy-to-libs`, which also prunes stale copies
and writes the `dom-renderer.current` pointer manifest the SSR layer reads to emit the
`<script src>`). Applications get the bundle automatically; the fresh URL per build
busts the immutable asset cache.

## Transport resilience

`src/transport.ts` reconnects with exponential backoff, keeps the connection
alive with a `META::PING`/`PONG` heartbeat + no-activity watchdog, and recovers
from lost deltas: a **sequence gap** (a batch whose per-stream `sequence` breaks
the chain) makes the client skip the gapped batch and request a full snapshot
(`META::RESYNC`). See `spec/OPCODE.md` §Transport heartbeat and §Sequence gap
detection.---

## A. Primitive Drawing & Visual Nodes

### Text — `TEXT` 0x01

A run of styled text. The server dictates content and style; the client measures
and renders.

---

`BORDER_EDGES` is a u32 bitmask (`SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type)
selecting which edges of a node's border are drawn. Bits are direction-aware:

| Bit | Mask | Edge | Physical (LTR) |
|-----|------|------|----------------|
| 0 | `0x00000001` | `TOP` | top |
| 1 | `0x00000002` | `LEADING` | left |
| 2 | `0x00000004` | `BOTTOM` | bottom |
| 3 | `0x00000008` | `TRAILING` | right |

protocol).

#### Semantic properties

Semantic properties describe a node's meaning and interaction state rather than
its layout or decoration. Currently exercised: `SELECTED` carries the boolean

# ADR-0014: Virtualized lazy stacks through app-owned data sources

**Status:** Accepted
**Recorded:** 2026-11-12
**Scope:** Authoring DSL, retained-tree emission, lazy-container layout, renderer realization, SSR first paint
**Supersedes:** None (refines the lazy-container realization wording in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`)

## Context

Lazy stack and grid component IDs exist (`LAZY_VSTACK`, `LAZY_HSTACK`,
`LAZY_VGRID`, `LAZY_HGRID`), but the protocol only says a renderer MAY defer
realizing off-screen children. No item count, extent, visible-range request, or
window placement exists, so every implementation treats lazy containers as eager
aliases. Two constraints make the current wording insufficient:

- The app emits the full child list, and the desktop ring (4096 slots) and arena
  (1 MiB) cannot carry thousands of rows.
- A renderer cannot position or size an unrealized row without a size model, so
  it cannot compute scroll extent or decide what is visible.

The authoring surface must remain SwiftUI-shaped (ADR-0013):
`LazyVStack(spacing:) { ForEach(items) { … } }`, not a parallel
`VirtualVStack`.

## Decision

Virtualize lazy stacks through an app-owned data source and a renderer-reported
visible range.

- `ForEach` inside a `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` is a data source, not an eager
  child list. Outside a lazy container it keeps eager behavior.
- The app supplies the item collection and row builder; the engine owns the
  visible window and materializes only the window's rows.
- Fixed uniform extent: the engine derives `ITEM_EXTENT` from the row's fixed
  main-axis frame (`.frame(height:)` / `.frame(width:)`), or from an explicit
  `itemExtent` when no fixed frame exists.
- The wire carries `ITEM_COUNT`, `ITEM_EXTENT`, and `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` on the
  lazy container; the renderer reports `VISIBLE_RANGE` (first index + count) for
  nodes that declare listener bit 10.
- The lazy container occupies the full virtual main-axis extent
  (`N*E + max(0,N-1)*S`); emitted child `j` is placed at
  `(FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j)*(E+S)`.
- Window children are reconciled by absolute index (or an optional item key), so
  ids stay stable while scrolling.
- SSR renders a conservative first window plus the full virtual extent; the
  client corrects the window after `META::ENVIRONMENT`.
- v1 covers `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK`; lazy grids follow the same model in a
  later change.

Exact requirements live in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`,
`spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, and `spec/DSL.md`.

## Rationale

- Only the window costs app nodes, wire bytes, renderer model memory, native
  elements, and SSR HTML; the full list can be arbitrarily large.
- The renderer stays stateless: it reports a measured/derived range, like
  `FIT_CHANGED`, and the app decides what to emit.
- The app-owned data source keeps the SwiftUI shape and avoids a second lazy
  authoring vocabulary.
- Fixed extent gives exact scroll extent and window math without measurement
  passes, matching the fixed-row-height pattern that avoids layout work.
- Windowed SSR avoids O(N) HTML while the full virtual extent keeps the
  scrollbar correct before JavaScript runs.

## Alternatives

- **Renderer-owned windowing with all children transmitted.** Rejected: O(N) app
  tree, wire, and renderer memory; overflows the desktop ring; cannot size
  unrealized rows; O(N) SSR.
- **Renderer pull by index.** Rejected for v1: adds a request/response handshake
  and renderer-owned item identity without removing the app's data-source work.
- **A separate `VirtualVStack`/`VirtualHStack` authoring API.** Rejected:
  confusing alongside `LazyVStack`, and contrary to the SwiftUI-shaped surface.
- **Variable-height first.** Deferred: needs estimation, measurement caching,
  and scroll anchoring; fixed extent covers the initial large-list use case.
- **Full SSR for every list.** Rejected as the default: O(N) HTML; remains
  available as an explicit host option for SEO-critical lists.

## Consequences

- New protocol properties (`ITEM_COUNT`, `ITEM_EXTENT`, `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX`),
  event (`VISIBLE_RANGE`), and listener bit (10) require Rust/Java/TS constants,
  manifest, codec, and conformance updates.
- The engine gains lazy-node window state and a keyed window reconcile;
  renderers gain virtual-extent placement and range reporting.
- Row-local component state is scoped by the `ForEach` item key and survives
  window eviction (follow-up implemented; spec/DSL.md §Virtualized lists).
- Lazy grids and variable-height rows are implemented; native recycling, scroll
  anchoring, and focused-row pinning remain follow-ups.
- The app must keep a focused row inside its window; the renderer does not
  auto-pin it.

## Sources and current contract

- Lazy container allocation: [PRIMITIVES.md §LazyVStack](../../spec/PRIMITIVES.md#lazyvstack--lazy_vstack-0x1b).
- Virtual extent and placement: [LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](../../spec/LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-containers).
- Event and listener: [EVENTS.md §Visible range](../../spec/EVENTS.md#visible-range), [§Event listeners](../../spec/EVENTS.md#event-listeners-event_listeners).
- Properties: [MODIFIERS.md §Layout](../../spec/MODIFIERS.md#1-layout).
- Authoring surface: [DSL.md §Virtualized lists](../../spec/DSL.md#virtualized-lists-lazyvstack--lazyhstack).
- Decisions: [ADR-0002](0002-native-declarative-layout.md),
  [ADR-0003](0003-application-state-and-delta-emission.md),
  [ADR-0011](0011-explicit-layout-allocation.md),
  [ADR-0013](0013-swiftui-shaped-signal-dsl.md).

- **Media swap coverage (MEDIA-COVERAGE-001):** `MediaProjectionTest` covers
  root projection, surface-first binding, root-rerender identity, and transport
  targeting. It does not establish every structural-swap frame invariant or
  native playback continuity. See the
  [traceability pilot audit](../../../docs/audits/media-controller-identity.md).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` containing
  a `ForEach` are windowed — extent inference, engine-owned window, keyed
  window reconcile, the window properties, and `VISIBLE_RANGE` routing are
  implemented; lazy grids use a row/column window over the same data source.
  Variable-height stacks are supported with app-declared `itemExtents`
  (`ITEM_EXTENTS`/`FIRST_ITEM_OFFSET`/`TOTAL_EXTENT`); grids use a uniform
  extent. Row-local `state(...)` is keyed by the `ForEach` item key and survives
  window eviction. The engine derives a bounded, directional prefetch from the
  `VISIBLE_RANGE` report velocity and decays to the base margin on a final
  report (ADR-0015); the author does not configure overscan. Gaps:
  focused-row pinning.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-core` is the pure-Java opcode/wire leaf: protocol, frame codec,
  events, opcode sink, attributed text, and Markdown.
- `pathland-view-core` is the Kotlin engine + DSL module: signal/state/router,
  the `View` SPI and value types, the retained-tree emitter, and
  `dev.pathland.view.dsl`. It depends on `pathland-core`.
- `core`/`engine`/`dsl` remain logical subpackages inside `pathland-view-core`,
  with a few deliberate intra-module references (`Color`/`MediaController`/

No related to Mac, but as question that probably brings some devs that try to implement keyboard navigation in Lists on iOS, there's how I managed to do that (let me know if there's a better way).
1. Create MyController: UIViewController that embeds your MySwiftView: View (that contains a List) in UIHostingController and ads it as a subview. Keep a reference to MySwiftView to pass keyboard events to MySwiftView
2. Implement support for keyboard commands (e.g. Enter, Escape and Up/down arrows) in MyController. See useyourloaf.com/blog/adding-hardware-keyboard-shortcuts/
3. Pass navigation commands to MySwiftView, and implement navigation logic in MySwiftView (or at the model that MySwiftView uses to display) data.

SwiftUI List vs LazyVStack

Every SwiftUI developer eventually hits this fork: you need to show a scrolling collection, and you can reach for List or for ScrollView + LazyVStack . Both are lazy. Both only build visible rows. So the choice looks like styling preference.
It isn't. They have genuinely different memory behavior, and the difference shows up exactly when you can least afford it - long collections on older devices.
The short version, with the reasoning below:
Use List by default. Reach for LazyVStack when you need a layout List can't express, and only after you've accepted that you're taking on memory management yourself.

...

What List Gives You for Free

Beyond recycling, List ships a large amount of behavior that's tedious to rebuild:

}
. listStyle (. insetGrouped )
. refreshable  {
     await  store. reload ()
}
. searchable (text:  $searchTerm )
Swipe-to-delete, drag-to-reorder, pull-to-refresh, separators, section headers that stick, selection and edit mode, and correct keyboard-avoidance behavior. Plus accessibility - VoiceOver announces "row 3 of 40" in a List automatically, and doesn't in a LazyVStack unless you add it yourself.

A Decision Table

* Need | Use
* Standard vertical rows | List
* Swipe actions, reorder, edit mode | List
* Pull to refresh | List ( .refreshable works on ScrollView too, but rest of the list features don't)
* Sections with sticky headers | Either
* Thousands of rows | List
* Free VoiceOver row semantics | List
* Mixed row types with custom spacing | LazyVStack
* Grid or horizontal scrolling | LazyVGrid / LazyHStack
* Scroll-linked visual effects | LazyVStack
* Bounded collection (< ~200 rows), custom design | Either, LazyVStack fine"

Issue body actions

## Context

ADR-0014 follow-up. Lazy stacks virtualize rows, but a focused control inside a row loses focus when the row scrolls out of the window and is evicted. The row (and its native element) is deleted, then recreated on re-entry.

**Chosen model:** Option A — focus observation plus a contiguous window union (no protocol change). Rust DSL parity is included in this issue.

## Problem

Two gaps:

1.  **Focus is not observable by the app.** Renderers emit `FOCUS_CHANGED` for nodes with `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit 5 (GTK `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:778`, DOM `lib/typescript/src/index.ts:390`; Qt currently only for text inputs, `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/qt_layer.cpp:3286`). The JVM host drops the event: `InputDispatcher` has no focus branch (`lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/kotlin/dev/pathland/view/engine/InputDispatcher.kt:38`), `RenderResult` has no focus map, `PathlandNode` has no focus callback, and the DSL has no `.onFocusChanged` (only `pointerEvents(mask)`).
2.  **The lazy window is contiguous.** `ITEM_COUNT`/`ITEM_EXTENT`/`FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` place emitted child `j` at `(FIRST_ITEM_INDEX+j)*(E+S)` (`spec/LAYOUT.md` §Virtual extent). A row outside the window cannot be "kept mounted" without expanding the contiguous range.

Keyed window reconcile (commit `0505b268`) keeps ids for rows that **remain** in the window; it does not keep an evicted row mounted.

## Proposed scope (Option A)

### Phase 1 — focus observation

JVM/web:

-   `PathlandNode.focusInput` (`Consumer<Boolean>?`).
-   `Emitter.focusInputs` (collect/clear like `editingInput`), exposed via `RenderResult.focusInputs`.
-   `InputDispatcher`: route `FOCUS_CHANGED` to `focusInputs[target]?.accept(b != 0)`.
-   DSL: `View.onFocusChanged { focused -> … }` (sets `Commands.Listeners.FOCUS` and `node.focusInput`).
-   Tests: mount with `.onFocusChanged`, dispatch `Event.focusChanged(target, true/false)`, assert the callback/signal and the emitted listener bit.
-   Spec: update `spec/DSL.md` §5.5 and `spec/MODIFIERS.md` §semantic.

Qt:

-   Report focus for any node with the FOCUS listener bit, not only text inputs. GTK/DOM already do.

### Phase 2 — pinned-row window union

-   `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` (and the underlying `ForEach`) take a pinned index/key signal.
-   `LazyStackView` reads the pin and unions it into `initialWindow` and the `VISIBLE_RANGE` window:  
    `window = (visibleStart - overscan) .. (visibleEnd + overscan)` ∪ `pinnedIndex`.
-   App wiring: a row's `.onFocusChanged` sets a `focusedIndex`/`focusedKey` signal; the lazy stack receives it.
-   The pin is cleared on focus loss.
-   Document the `O(gap)` behavior: the app should clear the pin when the row is more than N units outside the viewport.
-   Test: pin a far index, assert the window includes it and the row is emitted; clear, assert the window returns to the visible range.

### Phase 3 — Rust DSL parity

-   `Node.focus_input` + `InputHandlers.focus`; route `Event::FocusChanged` in the Rust demos.
-   `ForEach::pinned` (or an equivalent pinned-index handle).
-   `build_lazy_stack` unions the pinned index into the window.
-   Tests mirroring the JVM/web pin/window behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

-   A focusable row reports focus to the app on JVM/web (and GTK/Qt).
-   A focused row remains mounted when scrolled out of the visible window.
-   Focus survives an overlapping window slide; unpin on focus loss.
-   The window union is covered by JVM and Rust DSL tests; no regressions in lazy-stack/grid rendering or deltas.
-   Spec/status/ADR-0014 follow-up notes updated.

## References

-   ADR-0014, `spec/LAYOUT.md` §Virtual extent, `spec/EVENTS.md` §Text/`FOCUS_CHANGED`, `spec/DSL.md` §5.5/§Virtualized lists.
-   `lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/kotlin/dev/pathland/view/dsl/LazyList.kt`, `.../engine/InputDispatcher.kt`, `.../engine/RenderResult.kt`, `.../engine/PathlandNode.kt`.
-   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/src/lib.rs`, `lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/src/node.rs`.
-   Keyed reconcile: commit `0505b268`.

## Short answer

Yes — in SwiftUI this is automatic **only for `List`**, not for `ScrollView` + `LazyVStack`.

- `List(selection:)` on macOS moves the selection with ↑/↓ (and Home/End/Return) natively.
- `ScrollView { LazyVStack { … } }` does **not**. The SwiftUI pattern is `.focusable()` + `@FocusState` + `.onKeyPress` / `.onMoveCommand`, plus `ScrollViewReader`/`scrollPosition` to keep the selected row visible.

Pathland's demo uses the second shape (`LibraryView.kt:76-97`, rows are `HStack + onTapGesture` at `TrackRowView.kt:74-79`), so nothing gives arrow navigation for free. Tabbing probably reaches the `ScrollView` because Chrome 132+ makes scrollable overflow containers focusable — it is not becoming a real list keyboard target.

## What is missing today

- `InputDispatcher` drops `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` and `FOCUS_CHANGED` (`lib/java/.../InputDispatcher.kt:38`); `RenderResult` has no focus/key maps.
- The DSL only exposes raw `pointerEvents(mask)` — no `focusable`, `onFocusChanged`, or `onKeyPress` (`Modifiers.kt:448-449`).
- Renderers do not make app nodes focusable (`tabindex`, `set_focusable`, Qt activeFocus):
  - DOM only reports focus for text inputs (`lib/typescript/src/index.ts:360-399`), and SSR emits no `tabindex`.
  - GTK only handles window-level Escape/Backspace (`pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:3312-3333`); it attaches a focus controller but never makes the widget focusable.
  - Qt reports keys only for focused text inputs (`qt_layer.cpp:3286-3297`).
- `#204` covers focus observation + keeping a focused row inside the lazy window, but not making rows focusable, delivering keys, moving focus, or revealing the selection.

## Recommended shape (SwiftUI-like)

Treat this as **row focus with app-driven focus movement**, plus #204 as a prerequisite:

1. **#204 Phase 1** — `focusInputs` in `RenderResult`/`PathlandNode`/emitter, `InputDispatcher` routing, DSL `.onFocusChanged`, Qt generic focus reporting.
2. **DSL primitives** — `.focusable(...)`, `.onKeyPress(...)` (↑/↓/Home/End/Enter/Space), a `FocusState`/focus request analog of `@FocusState`.
3. **Renderer support** — make focusable nodes real tab stops; report `FOCUS_CHANGED` for them; forward canonical `KEY_DOWN/UP`; implement a small focus command so the app can move focus to the next row (native focus then scrolls it into view). Canonicalize key codes across DOM/GTK/Qt.
4. **#204 Phase 2** — union the focused index into the lazy window so the row survives eviction; clear on focus loss.
5. **Demo** — add `focusedIndex`; make only the focused row the single tab stop (roving focus); arrows move `focusedIndex`, Enter plays; parent gets `ROLE=List`; focused row emits `SELECTED`/focus state; keep the playing row visually distinct from the focused row.
6. **Tests/docs** — engine/dispatcher tests, DOM vitest, GTK/Qt headless tests, lazy window union tests, and updates to `spec/DSL.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, status files, and `#204`.

A smaller alternative is a **single focusable list container** plus a `SCROLL_TO` command: the app handles arrows on the container and asks the renderer to reveal the selected row. It touches fewer focus semantics but gives a list-level focus ring rather than row focus.

Either real solution needs one small wire addition (a focus request or scroll-to command); #204 alone deliberately has none, so it cannot deliver arrow navigation by itself.

/**
 * The music player demo: a track library, now-playing sidebar with album art,
 * and a bottom player bar. Asserts the rendered tree and that interactions drive
 * the persisted player state.

class MusicPlayerViewTest {

    private data class Mounted(
        val result: RenderResult,
        val sink: FrameOpcodeSink,
        val store: StateStore,
    )

    private class MultiFrameSink : FrameOpcodeSink() {
        val frames = mutableListOf<ProtocolFrame>()

        override fun endFrame() {
            super.endFrame()
            frames.add(frame())
        }
    }

    private fun mount(snapshot: Boolean = false): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val state = PersistentState(store, "session-1")
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        if (snapshot) emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    private fun mountAd(): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(
            MusicPlayerView.make("http://localhost:8080/ad"),
            Environment(PersistentState(store, "session-1")),
        )
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    @Test
    fun libraryRendersTracksAndAlbumArt() {
        val frame = mount().sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Building on Solid Ground"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Rendered Free"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Pathland Dream"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Foundation"))
        assertFalse(anySetText(frame, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Library"))
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.IMAGE) >= 3)

# Architecture traceability and drift

This workflow connects implementation to the current contract and decision
rationale. A reference identifies what governs code; it is **not a certification
that the code complies**. Specs remain authoritative for requirements, ADRs for
decision history, and per-project `status.md` for implementation coverage.

## Source references

Put a standalone comment near the relevant declaration or implementation block:

```rust
// @ref spec/MEDIA.md#5-structural-swaps-the-motivating-contract [implements]
```

Use a repository-root-relative Markdown path, an optional heading fragment,
a required relation, and an optional short gloss following an em dash:

```text
@ref path/to/document.md#heading [relation] — Short explanation
```

| Relation | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `implements` | Implements the referenced requirement |
| `tests` | Exercises the requirement; does not imply exhaustive coverage |
| `constrained-by` | Shaped by an architectural constraint or decision |
| `explains` | Context, not a claim of implementation |
| `historical` | Deliberate reference to retired guidance, not a current constraint |

Normally code/tests point to a **specific spec section**, and that section links
to its ADR. Link directly to an ADR when the architectural boundary itself is
what matters. Use `historical` only for genuine historical context, not to bypass
updating an implementation's governing reference. Proposed ADRs cannot be
implementation constraints until accepted by a maintainer.

Keep directives in source comments (`//`, `///`, `//!`, block-comment `*`, or
`#`), not string literals. References are human-placed breadcrumbs, not
compiler-enforced attachments. The checker validates standalone directive lines;
it does not parse language syntax or prove which declaration a comment governs.
Use normal Markdown links in documentation. This is Pathland's convention,
inspired by LLP, not compatibility with the upstream LLP skill contracts.

## Adoption and change review

- Prioritize non-obvious invariants, architectural boundaries, and behavior an
  agent might otherwise simplify incorrectly. Do not annotate every function.
- Add accurate references when touching governed code; review scope and target
  meaning, not just whether the path exists.
- Requirement changes include spec updates and behavioral tests. Significant
  architectural changes also propose a new ADR, superseding the prior record
  only after maintainer acceptance.
- Keep references, contract changes, tests, and affected `status.md` updates
  together. Do not mechanically annotate files without reviewing their behavior.
- Existing unreferenced code is a review backlog, not an automatic CI failure.

## Drift resolution

Do not assume the code or the document is right merely because it is newer.
Report the discrepancy before changing the governing decision.

| Finding | Resolution |
|---------|------------|
| Code violates a still-valid contract | Fix the implementation and add a regression test |
| Spec misstates intended behavior | Propose a correction and assess compatibility; do not silently bless the code |
| Architecture intentionally changes | Propose a superseding ADR, then coordinate specs, code, and tests |
| Reference is inaccurate or stale | Repair the reference; investigate whether behavior also drifted |
| Intent is uncertain or documents conflict | Record evidence and request a maintainer decision |
| Requirement lacks adequate tests | Record the coverage gap separately from a demonstrated violation |

A finding records: an identifier, audit date and source revision, governing
spec/ADR, implementation symbols, observed behavior, reproduction or test
evidence, existing coverage, and proposed resolution. Distinguish static review,
executed tests, and hypotheses. Never claim a test ran when it did not.

Store cross-project audit reports under `docs/audits/`. Put unresolved
implementation gaps in affected projects' `status.md`, linking to the report;
the audit is evidence, not a competing implementation-status system. Resolve
findings explicitly with a linked fix or a maintainer-approved contract change.
An audit is a dated snapshot, not an automatically current conformance claim.

# Skill: pathland-decision

# Pathland decision authoring

## Trigger

When asked to capture a consequential choice, extract established rationale, or
propose replacing an architectural decision. If the problem or intended choice
is unclear, ask before allocating a number. A request to discuss a decision is
not permission to write files.

## Invariants

- Follow [ADR conventions](../../../docs/decisions/README.md#conventions), the
  [template](../../../docs/decisions/template.md), and
  [drift rules](../../../docs/decisions/traceability.md#drift-resolution).
- New ADRs start **Proposed**. Never accept, reject, or supersede on the
  maintainer's behalf. The initial extraction's Accepted status is not a
  precedent for agent approval of new decisions.
- Preserve accepted decision history. A material reversal needs a new record;
  factual corrections do not require manufacturing a new architectural choice.
- Do not duplicate requirements into ADRs or quietly rewrite specs to legitimize
  drift. A proposed decision does not change the current contract.
- Separate documented evidence, maintainer-confirmed reasoning (with attribution
  and date), and unconfirmed hypotheses. Never invent historical alternatives,
  benchmarks, original dates, or approval.
- Do not overwrite existing files, install upstream LLP, or create its hierarchy.

## Workflow

1. Locate the repository root and read the relevant instructions, ADR index,
   current spec sections, and existing decisions. Use `pathland-orient`'s method
   if context is missing; source paths below are repository-root-relative.
2. Check whether this is already covered, a factual correction, or a new choice.
   For an existing accepted decision, propose a correction or superseding record
   rather than rewriting the historical choice in place.
3. When authorized to draft a file, allocate the next `NNNN` after the highest
   number in current ADR filenames **and locally available Git history**:
   inspect `git log --all --name-only --format= -- docs/decisions` as well as
   current/untracked files. Never reuse deleted numbers. In a shallow or partial
   history, disclose uncertainty and ask before assuming an allocation is safe;
   do not fetch without authorization. Branch numbers remain provisional until
   integration; resolve collisions before merge.
4. Create `docs/decisions/NNNN-short-name.md` using the template. Use the actual
   recording date, affected scope, and a linked `Supersedes` field where relevant.
   Draft context, decision, rationale, alternatives, consequences, and sources.
   For extraction, identify the source revision and unknown historical details.
5. Add the Proposed record to the ADR index. Link to current contracts, but do
   not present proposed requirements as already normative or retire an accepted
   predecessor. Describe the spec/code/test/status updates acceptance would need.
6. Review local paths/anchors and the diff. Run the reference checker if source
   references changed. Stop at the proposal; no commit/push or implementation
   unless separately requested.

## Artifact

Return the proposed ADR (in conversation or authorized file), its status and
allocated path, supporting evidence, open questions, alternatives not yet
evaluated, and the integration checklist. Identify any author-confirmation gaps.

## Hand-offs

- `pathland-review` evaluates the proposal; it does not approve it.
- The maintainer decides acceptance/rejection. Only after explicit acceptance
  should the requested implementation update supersession links, the index,
  current specs, code references, tests, and affected `status.md` together.
- If this was an implementation defect rather than a new choice, use
  `pathland-maintain` to classify the drift instead of creating a justifying ADR.

## Plan: keyboard-navigable track list (web first)

### Decision summary

SwiftUI gives this for free only with `List(selection:)`; `ScrollView` + `LazyVStack` requires `.focusable()` + `@FocusState` + `.onKeyPress`/`.onMoveCommand`. Pathland's demo uses the latter shape, so we implement the equivalent explicitly:

- **Model:** one roving tab stop on the focused row; ↑/↓ move focus; Enter plays.
- **Mechanism:** app-driven focus request + #204 pinning. Follows `@FocusState`, not renderer-owned list behavior.
- **Scope:** JVM/web now (Spring/Quarkus + DOM). GTK/Qt and Rust DSL parity remain follow-ups on #204.

Because a new wire command is required, the first step is a **Proposed ADR**; implementation of the command waits for maintainer acceptance.

---

## Phase 0 — Proposed ADR (gate)

Add `docs/decisions/0018-app-driven-focus-requests.md` as **Proposed**, plus the ADR index entry.

Recommend:

- `META::SET_FOCUS` `0x09`, guest → host: `A = nodeId`, `B = 1` focus / `0` clear.
- Renderer applies it **after** tree/property deltas so the target is materialized and focusable first.
- Focus remains renderer state; `FOCUS_CHANGED` remains the observation event.
- Canonical key-code table in `spec/EVENTS.md`.

Alternatives to record: renderer-owned `ROLE=List` navigation, a `FOCUSED` property instead of a command, `SCROLL_TO`/reveal instead of focus, and Tab-only with no wire change.

Do not implement the wire command until accepted.

---

## Phase 1 — #204 focus observation (JVM/web)

Implement the no-wire-change half of #204:

- `PathlandNode.focusInput: Consumer<Boolean>?`.
- `Emitter.focusInputs` collection/clearing, exposed through `RenderResult.focusInputs`.
- `InputDispatcher` routes `FOCUS_CHANGED` → `focusInputs[target]?.accept(b != 0)` (`InputDispatcher.kt:38` currently has no branch).
- DSL `View.onFocusChanged { focused -> … }` sets the `FOCUS` listener bit.
- Tests: listener bit, callback routing, `RenderResult` map, clear-on-eviction.

Qt generic focus reporting and Rust DSL parity stay on #204 as follow-ups.

---

## Phase 2 — #204 pinned-row window union (JVM/web)

- Add `pin: Signal<Int?>?` (or keyed equivalent) to `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` and `LazyStackView`.
- In `LazyStackView.renderNode`, union the pinned index with the visible window for **emitted children only**; do not overwrite `windowSignal`.
- Union into `initialWindow` too.
- Add an app-visible range hook (e.g. `onVisibleRange`) so the demo can clamp a far-away pin:
  - keep the pin while the row is focused/near the viewport;
  - when the list is unfocused and the row is far outside, move the focused index to the visible edge so the app never emits an O(N) gap.
- Ensure `PagedForEach` prefetch covers the union but is bounded by that policy.
- Tests: pin a far index → row emitted; clear pin → window returns; paged/placeholder behavior; no window-signal corruption.
- Update #204 with JVM/web completion and remaining Qt/Rust items.

---

## Phase 3 — Focus + keyboard primitives (after ADR acceptance)

Protocol/core:

- Add `meta::SET_FOCUS` to Rust constants, JVM `Commands.Meta`, TS `CMD_SET_FOCUS`; regenerate `spec/protocol.tsv`.
- Add `setFocus(nodeId, focused)` to `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`, `RingOpcodeSink`.
- Add key-code constants/mapping (arrows `37–40`, Home `36`, End `35`, PageUp `33`, PageDown `34`, Enter `13`, Space `32`, Tab `9`, Escape `27`, Backspace `8`, Delete `46`, letters/digits ASCII).
- Update `spec/OPCODE.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, manifest and manifest test.

DSL/engine:

- `Keys` + `KeyEvent`.
- `View.focusable(enabled: Boolean = true)` — declares `FOCUS` and makes the node a tab stop.
- `View.focused(focused: Signal<Boolean>)` — emits/reconciles `SET_FOCUS`.
- `View.onKeyDown { event -> … }` — declares `KEY_DOWN`, stores a per-node key handler (KEY_UP deferred).
- `PathlandNode.keyInput`, `Emitter.keyInputs`, `RenderResult.keyInputs`, `InputDispatcher` key branch.
- Focus effect: emit `SET_FOCUS` at the end of the frame's deltas; avoid duplicate requests.
- Tests: handler registration/routing, focus request opcode, focus/focusable bit emission, removal.

---

## Phase 4 — Web renderers

HTML SSR (Java `HtmlRenderer` + Rust canonical parity):

- `event_attrs` adds `tabindex="0"` when the `FOCUS` bit is set.
- Set `tabindex="-1"` on `SCROLLVIEW` unless it itself declares `FOCUS`, so Chrome’s scroll-container focusability does not add an extra tab stop.
- Add a golden SSS fixture for a focusable lazy-list row; regenerate with `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`.
- Update Java golden parity.

DOM client (`lib/typescript`):

- `PROP_EVENT_LISTENERS` adds/removes `tabindex` based on the `FOCUS` bit.
- `focusin`/`focusout` report `FOCUS_CHANGED` for **any** node with the `FOCUS` bit, not only text inputs.
- `keydown`/`keyup` resolve the active element, send canonical key codes.
- `preventDefault` for navigation keys when the target declares `KEY_DOWN`; leave Tab alone.
- Apply `META::SET_FOCUS` via `element.focus()`.
- Add focus-ring styling for `[tabindex]` rows in the design layer; rebuild/sync CSS.
- Tests: tabindex toggling, generic focus reporting, key mapping/preventDefault, focus command application.
- Build and copy the bundle (`npm run build:all`).

---

## Phase 5 — Demo wiring

Keep focus state in `MediaPlayerService` (not `LibraryView`) because `PlayerMainArea` is instantiated once per `ViewThatFits` candidate; a per-component signal would reset on a layout swap.

- `service.focusedIndex = Signals.signal(0)` (ephemeral, not persisted).
- In `LibraryView`, apply a shared row wrapper to **both** loaded and placeholder rows:
  - `.focusable(active)` and `.focused(active)` only on the focused row → single tab stop.
  - `.onFocusChanged { if (it) service.focusedIndex.set(index) }`.
  - `.onKeyDown`: ↑/↓ adjust within `0..total-1`; Enter calls `selectTrack(index)`; Space optionally toggles playback.
- Pass `pin = service.focusedIndex` to `LazyVStack`.
- Keep the playing-row highlight (`trackIndex`) distinct from the focused row; the renderer owns the focus ring, the app may add a subtle focused-row background.
- Add `ROLE=List` around the lazy list; rows already use `LIST_ITEM`.
- v1 intentionally omits Home/End/PageUp/PageDown because they force an O(gap) window union without a scroll-to primitive.
- Tests: initial single tab stop, key dispatch moves focus and emits `SET_FOCUS`, Enter plays, placeholder pin, focus survives a window slide.

---

## Phase 6 — Documentation and follow-ups

Update specs and status files together:

- `spec/OPCODE.md`, `EVENTS.md`, `DSL.md`, `MODIFIERS.md`, `PRIMITIVES.md`, `LAYOUT.md`, `CONFORMANCE.md`.
- ADR-0018 (if accepted) and ADR-0014 follow-up notes.
- `status.md` for JVM view-core, Java/Rust HTML renderers, TypeScript, demo views, core constants.
- `AGENTS.md` “In progress” status if focused-row pinning/keyboard nav lands.

Follow-ups:

- GTK/Qt: make `FOCUS`-bit widgets focusable/add key controllers, forward canonical keys, implement `SET_FOCUS`, report generic focus.
- Rust DSL: `focus_input`/`key_input`, pin, focus request, engine traces.
- `KEY_UP`, Home/End/Page, type-ahead, and a reusable SwiftUI-`List`-shaped composite helper.
- Possible later `SCROLL_TO`/`SCROLL_POSITION` for large jumps.

---

## Verification

```bash
cd lib/rust && cargo test
cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --check

cd lib/java && mvn -P jvm-only install
cd lib/typescript && npm test && npm run build:all

python3 scripts/check-references.py
```

Manual: run the Spring/Quarkus demo, Tab into the library, ↑/↓ across page boundaries, Enter to play, Tab out and back, resize across fit breakpoints, and confirm focus/scroll survives.

## Key risks

- **ADR gate:** the wire command must not land before maintainer acceptance.
- **O(gap):** pinning a far row defeats virtualization; bounded/clamp policy is required.
- **Placeholder rows:** focus/key modifiers must be applied to the paged `placeholder` path too.
- **Extra tab stop:** Chrome may focus the scroll container; `tabindex="-1"` is needed.
- **Focus vs playback:** keep the focused row and playing row visually/semantically distinct.
- **Browser differences:** scroll-container focusability and `preventDefault` behavior vary; key handling should not depend on browser defaults.

# ADR-NNNN: Decision title

**Status:** Proposed
**Recorded:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Scope:** Affected architectural areas
**Supersedes:** None (or a linked ADR)

## Context

What problem or constraint requires a decision?

## Decision

What is the chosen approach? For a proposal, what is being proposed?
Link to the specification for exact requirements rather than defining them here.

## Rationale

Why this approach? Distinguish documented evidence, maintainer-confirmed
reasoning, and unconfirmed hypotheses. Do not infer historical intent from code.

## Alternatives

What alternatives were actually considered, and why were they not selected?
Say when the historical evaluation is not documented.

## Consequences

Benefits, costs, limitations, and implications of the choice.

## Sources and current contract

Link supporting documents and the current specification. For an extraction,
identify its source and extraction date; do not fabricate an original date.
---
# Architecture decision records

ADRs explain **why** Pathland makes consequential architectural choices.
[`spec/`](../../spec/) defines the **current contract**; each implementing
project's `status.md` tracks **implementation coverage**. ADRs do not introduce
additional mandatory behavior or replace either source of truth.

## Index

| ADR | Decision | Status |
|-----|----------|--------|
| [0001](0001-fixed-width-binary-protocol.md) | Fixed-width binary instructions and transport-independent frames | Accepted |
| [0002](0002-native-declarative-layout.md) | Declarative structure and native renderer-owned layout | Accepted |
| [0003](0003-application-state-and-delta-emission.md) | Application-owned state and diff-based emission | Accepted |
| [0004](0004-binary-input-events.md) | Binary input events rather than payload callbacks | Accepted |
| [0005](0005-semantic-appearance.md) | Application intent and renderer-owned appearance | Accepted |
| [0006](0006-media-controller-identity.md) | Playback identity separate from media surfaces | Accepted |
| [0007](0007-portable-protocol-core.md) | Portable, emitter-free protocol core | Accepted |
| [0008](0008-pure-jvm-server-libraries.md) | Pure-JVM server libraries with opt-in native interop | Accepted |
| [0009](0009-cross-language-conformance.md) | Language-owned bindings checked by shared conformance data | Accepted |
| [0010](0010-server-side-proxy-composition.md) | Server-side composition through ordinary protocol sessions | Accepted |
| [0011](0011-explicit-layout-allocation.md) | Explicit Fixed/Fill/Hug allocation rather than implicit stretching | Accepted |
| [0012](0012-generated-html-base-design.md) | One generated, token-layered HTML base design | Accepted |
| [0013](0013-swiftui-shaped-signal-dsl.md) | SwiftUI-shaped authoring with signal-based reactivity | Accepted |
| [0014](0014-virtualized-lazy-stacks.md) | Virtualized lazy stacks through app-owned data sources | Accepted |
| [0015](0015-reactive-lazy-prefetch.md) | Engine-derived reactive prefetch for lazy windows | Accepted |
| [0016](0016-async-paged-data-sources.md) | Framework-neutral async and paged data sources for lists | Proposed |
| [0017](0017-visible-range-coalescing.md) | Latest-wins coalescing of lazy visible-range reports | Proposed |

## Conventions

Source-reference syntax, review obligations, drift resolution, and validation
commands are defined in [Architecture traceability and drift](traceability.md).
The [Pathland architecture skills](skills.md) provide reusable orientation,
decision-authoring, review, and maintenance workflows for these conventions.

- Use `NNNN-short-decision-name.md`, allocated sequentially. Never reuse a
  published number. Resolve provisional number collisions before merging.
- Start with [the template](template.md). Keep context, decision, rationale,
  alternatives, consequences, and source links distinct.
- Status is **Proposed**, **Accepted**, **Rejected**, or **Superseded**. A
  proposal is not binding; only a maintainer can accept a new decision.
- Accepted records preserve decision history. Correct factual errors in place;
  change a decision through a new ADR and mark the old one Superseded, linking
  both records. Update the index and current specs in the same change.
- Link ADRs to the relevant specs, and specs back to the ADRs. Keep complete
  requirements in specs so readers need not follow rationale links to find them.
- `AGENTS.md` retains essential guardrails and points here for rationale.
  READMEs retain orientation and usage instructions.
- Do not invent alternatives, benchmarks, author approval, or recovered intent.
  Identify uncertainty explicitly; an uncertain new proposal stays Proposed.

## Initial extraction provenance

ADRs 0001–0013 were extracted on **2026-11-12** from existing specifications,
READMEs, and `AGENTS.md`. Their Accepted status records decisions already
expressed by those sources; it does not claim a new approval or an original
decision date. Each record links its evidence. Consequences describe implications
of the documented choice, not a reconstructed historical evaluation.

# ADR-0017: Latest-wins coalescing of lazy visible-range reports

**Status:** Proposed
**Recorded:** 2026-11-17
**Scope:** Lazy-window input handling, paged data sources, DOM client, server runtime
**Supersedes:** None (extends ADR-0014/ADR-0015)

## Context

A windowed lazy stack reports `EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` when its visible range
changes. A fast scrollbar drag can produce a report every animation frame across
a large distance. The engine applies each report to the window, and a paged data
source loads the pages covering every intermediate window. On a long list this
can load much or all of the dataset for a gesture the user never paused on,
competing with the final window's pages and delaying it.

Only the latest visible range in a continuous input burst is useful for
rendering and prefetch: intermediate ranges are already off-screen by the time
their pages arrive.

## Decision

Treat successive visible-range reports for the same target as a latest-wins
stream:

- The DOM client throttles scroll/resize-driven reports to at most one per
  ~100 ms and still sends a final report when the gesture ends. Reports after
  hydration, batch application, or connection open stay immediate.
- The server runtime MAY coalesce reports per `(session, target)` for a short
  interval (~50 ms) before dispatching to the session actor; non-range events
  dispatch immediately.
- A paged data source applies only the current requested window. A page result
  that arrives after the window moved is cached (bounded) for a later return,
  but does not bump the render version for the current window and cannot add
  rows outside it; a stale failure does not change the visible loading/error
  state.

Exact behavior lives in [EVENTS.md §Visible range](../../spec/EVENTS.md#visible-range),
[LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](../../spec/LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-containers),
and [DSL.md §Virtualized lists](../../spec/DSL.md#virtualized-lists-lazyvstack--lazyhstack).

# ADR-0018: App-driven focus requests for keyboard navigation

**Status:** Proposed
**Recorded:** 2026-11-20
**Scope:** Wire protocol (`META`), JVM/Rust/TypeScript bindings, authoring DSL, HTML/DOM renderers, lazy-stack focus pinning
**Supersedes:** None (extends ADR-0004 and ADR-0014)

## Context

Pathland has raw keyboard events and focus observation, but no way for an
application to move renderer focus. A focused row can report `KEY_DOWN` and
`FOCUS_CHANGED`, yet an app-side handler cannot move focus to the next row.
Composed lists therefore cannot implement the keyboard navigation that a native
SwiftUI `List(selection:)` gets from its control implementation.

The music-player demo's library is `ScrollView` + `LazyVStack` with rows built
from `HStack` + `onTapGesture`. The rows are not focusable and the host drops
`KEY_DOWN`/`FOCUS_CHANGED`. Tabbing can reach the scrollable container in some
browsers, but the list has no roving row focus, no arrow navigation, and no way
to keep a focused row mounted while the lazy window slides.

Alternative approaches were considered but are not the selected model here:

- Let renderers interpret `ROLE=List` and implement arrow-key focus traversal
  themselves. This makes semantic structure behavioral and puts list navigation
  policy in every renderer.
- Represent focus as an app-owned `FOCUSED` property. Focus is renderer state;
  a one-shot request is clearer than a two-way state property.
- Add a `SCROLL_TO`/reveal command only. It can scroll a selection into view but
  does not establish focus, native focus rings, or accessible roving focus.
- Make every row tabbable and use only Tab. This does not provide arrow-key list
  navigation and creates an unbounded tab order for large lists.

## Decision

Add a guest-to-host focus request and keep focus itself renderer-owned:

- `META::SET_FOCUS` requests focus for one node (`A` = node id; `B` = 1 to focus,
  0 to clear). It is applied after the frame's structural and property deltas so
  the target can be materialized and focusable first.
- Focus remains renderer state. Renderers continue to report actual focus with
  `EVENT::FOCUS_CHANGED` for nodes that declared the `FOCUS` listener bit.
- Declaring the `FOCUS` listener bit makes a node focusable/tabbable; the app
  uses that to provide a single roving tab stop on the selected row.
- Apps observe focus with `.onFocusChanged`, handle keys with `.onKeyDown`, and
  request focus by binding `.focused(...)` to the target row.
- Canonical key codes are defined by the specification and shared by the DOM,
  GTK, and Qt renderers.
- ADR-0014's focused-row pinning keeps the focused row in the lazy window. Apps
  must bound the pin so a far-away focused row cannot defeat virtualization.

Exact requirements belong in the specifications (see "Sources and current
contract"); this record only fixes the architectural direction.

## Rationale

- The protocol already models raw input and focus observation; a focus request
  completes the same renderer-owned interaction loop without making renderers
  own application selection or list policy.
- A one-shot request matches the existing imperative `META` control commands and
  avoids a retained two-way focus property that would need reconciliation with
  native Tab traversal.
- A single roving tab stop mirrors the SwiftUI `List`/`@FocusState` authoring
  model: the app owns the selected key, native focus follows it, and the
  renderer owns the focus ring.
- Keeping the focus target mounted through ADR-0014's window union prevents the
  focused native element from being deleted and recreated while focus moves.

The SwiftUI `List` vs `ScrollView`/`LazyVStack` behavior and the demo's current
structure are documented evidence. The choice of a focus request over the listed
alternatives is a proposal, not an inferred historical decision.

## Alternatives

- **Renderer-owned list navigation:** fewer moving parts for app authors, but
  makes `ROLE` behavioral, duplicates navigation policy in every renderer, and
  limits app control over selection and activation.
- **`FOCUSED` property:** declarative, but focus is exclusive renderer state and
  would create a two-way property/Tab-focus reconciliation problem.
- **`SCROLL_TO` only:** simpler scroll reveal, but no focus, no native focus
  ring, and no assistive-technology focus movement.
- **Tab-only traversal:** no new wire surface, but not the requested behavior and
  impractical for long virtualized lists.

## Consequences

- Adds one `META` command and a canonical key-code contract across language
  bindings, with the usual manifest, conformance, spec, and status updates.
- Requires the JVM engine, Rust core, DOM client, and HTML renderers to agree on
  focusability and key delivery; GTK and Qt parity are follow-ups.
- Lazy stacks gain an app-supplied pin and a bounded union policy. Without the
  bound, pinning a far-away row emits the whole O(gap) window.
- Apps must keep focus and playback/selection distinct where they differ.
- A Proposed decision does not change the current contract until accepted.

## Sources and current contract

- Keyboard and focus events: [EVENTS.md §Keyboard](../../spec/EVENTS.md#keyboard),
  [§Text/FOCUS_CHANGED](../../spec/EVENTS.md#text).
- Control commands: [OPCODE.md §META commands](../../spec/OPCODE.md#meta-commands).
- Focusable/list authoring: [DSL.md §Interaction & state](../../spec/DSL.md#55-interaction--state),
  [MODIFIERS.md §5 Interaction & State](../../spec/MODIFIERS.md#5-interaction--state).
- List composition: [PRIMITIVES.md §Composite views](../../spec/PRIMITIVES.md#composite-views-not-primitives).
- Lazy window: [LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](../../spec/LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-containers),
  [ADR-0014](0014-virtualized-lazy-stacks.md).
- Input history: [ADR-0004](0004-binary-input-events.md).
- Follow-up: [PathlandDev/Pathland#204](https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/issues/204).

`PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`): each opcode sets one platform environment field, so
any number of fields ride one batch and new fields are new ids — never new
commands. The platform (renderer / DOM client / SSR host) delivers the
application's launch context this way; an HTTP request supplies what it offers,
and the WebSocket connection **enriches** the environment after connect
(viewport, native deep-links, and future fields all arrive the same way).

| `ROUTE` | `0x0003` | string offset | The initial route/deep-link path. String convention is the `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` dual: absolute offset into the host → guest **event arena** over the shared ring, *relative* offset into the batch's string section over the network. |

from the HTTP request (`ROUTE` = request path — all the request offers); over

router hydrates from the `ROUTE` field before mount, so a deep-link renders

new ids, never new commands. The protocol defines the concept; **each renderer

| `LOCALE` | `0x0003` | string offset | BCP 47 content locale |

absolute offset into the guest arena over the shared ring, or a *relative*
